caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 835 of 1991.
lawyer:
Md. Matiar Rahman with Md. Zakir Hossain and Quazi Aulad Hossain, Advocates ----- For the Plaintiff-Appellant. 
Md. Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For Defendant-Respondent No. 2
parties:
Hosne Ara Begum   ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Government of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and another ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque, J.: This First Appeal is directed against the judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No. 9 of 1985 by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, dismissing the suit. 

 2. Plaintiff is the appellant before this Court. Plaintiff claims right and title over the suit property by purchase. We need not go into the detailed discussions in respect of right and title of the plaintiff in view of the fact that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 222 of 1976 and in that title suit she got a decree and it was declared that the suit property cannot be treated and declared as an enemy property, It is also on record that in the year 1969 the property in question was treated as enemy/vested property by the Vested Property Authority who leased out the same to different lessees. Ultimately the matter came before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court where the defendants, namely, the Government and the Vested Property Authority lost the case and the decree obtained by the plaintiff in the Title Suit was maintained. This matter has also been discussed by the trial Court in this suit and the trial Court found that it was not required for it to consider the question of title, since the matter went up to the highest Court of the country which settled it once and for all. 

 After giving calculation in the aforesaid paragraph the plaintiff prayed for a decree for a sum of Tk. 83,61,000.00 with a prayer that till the property is not released in her favour she will be entitled to monthly rent at rate of Tk. 20,000.00. 

 8. As regards documentary evidence it appears that the plaintiff submitted so many documents in order to prove her case. Exts 1 (Ka) are the two registered kabalas in favor of the plaintiff Exts 2 to 4 (jha) are all the certified copies of different orders of different courts including High Court Division and Appellate Division which show that this matter went up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court with regard La the declaration of enemy property and ultimately the highest court of the country upheld the judgment and decree to the effect that this is not an enemy property. Ext. 5 is a letter dated 14.11.83 issued from the office of the Chief Martial Law Administrator by which the Martial Law Authority directed the Deputy Commissioner to take appropriate legal action in this matter in view of the fact that the plaintiff acquired title through the court upon the suit property Exts. 6 to 6(g) are the SA parcha of the suit property in which the name of the plaintiff was recorded. Ext. 7 is a letter issued from the Dhaka Pourashava. Ext. 8 is the letter vide office Memo No. 1106 (En.) VP. Ext. 8 (Ka) to 8 (cha) all are the letters to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka. From the side of the defendants some papers were filed before the Court which were marked as exhibits. Ext. A is the certified copy of the deed of gift executed by Sree Kallasha Chandra Shaha in favour of Sree Shontasha Kumar Shaha and another. Ext. B is the certified copy of the decree in Title Suit No. 32 of 1959 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Ext. C is the allotment letter of Memo No. 3005(11) E.P. dated 3.10.69. These are more or less-oral as well as documentary evidence as adduced by the parties. 

 9. We have stated above that the present suit has been filed claiming some damage, compensation and mesne profits over the suit property, It is the case of the plaintiff that she got a decree on 7.3.77 and filed that present suit on 6.3.85 So, at the rate of Tk. 20,000.00 per month she is claiming the compensation in the form of rent amounting to Tk. 21,60,000.00. In paragraph 16 of plaint it is asserted that for 65 rooms in the two suits buildings minimum monthly rent will come to Taka 20,000.00. That means the plaintiff is claiming compensation in the form of monthly rent of the 65 rooms of the two buildings. Now let us see what evidence the plaintiff has led before the Court in support of such claim. This assertion is made in paragraph 16 of the plaint. The plaintiff examined hereself as PW 1. In her deposition she also stated that monthly rent for the 65 rooms will be at least Tk. 20,000.00 and comparing the other neighboring buildings she made an assessment of rent of the disputed buildings. It is admitted position that the Government took over the suit property in the year 1969 as enemy/vested property and the Government leased out the same to the different lessees who paid rent to the Government from 1969. Mr. Shahidul Alam Chowdhury the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant respondent No. 2, very fairly submits that the defendant-respondent cannot challenge the right and title of the suit property in view of the fact that the matter went upto the Appellate Division and it was finally decided. So, in this Money Suit it is difficult for the defendant-respondents to challenge the right over the suit property. Further, it appears from the record that the plaintiff obtained decree in the year 1977 and the defendant-respondents went upto the Appellate Division but were unsuccessful. But they did not issue any release order of the suit property from the list of enemy/vested property list in favour of the plaintiff, though the plaintiff’s right and title had been accepted upto the highest court of the country. The learned Advocate further submits that he could not produce any paper to show before this court that the defendant-respondent had issued any order or letter releasing or dropping the suit property from the list of enemy/vested property which means till today the defendant-respondents have been possessing the suit property. Since the decree was obtained by the plaintiff in 1977 and since the defendant-respondents were unsuccessful even in the highest court of the country they ought to have issued a release order in favour of the plaintiff. So, we are of the view that the plaintiff is entitled to get compensation in the form of rent on the disputed property. 

 13. Before parting with the case we may observe that since the plaintiffs right and title have been settled by the highest Court of the country and since the defendant-respondents being responsible officers of the Government have been managing and possessing the suit property since 1969 and since the decree was obtained by the plaintiff in the year 1977, it is desirable that the officers of the Government should take proper steps for releasing the property in favour of the plaintiff immediately inasmuch as it is no more an enemy property in the eye of law and the defendant-respondents have no lawful authority to keep possession of the suit property anymore. In this connection we may refer to Ext. 5 which has been produced by the plaintiff. In the year 1983 the plaintiff made a representation to the Chief Martial Law Administrator for releasing the suit property stating the entire fact of getting a decree from the Court over the suit property. In pursuance of such representation the office of the Chief Martial Law Administrator wrote to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, by a letter dated 14.11.83 to the effect that after perusal of the certified copy of the court's judgment it appears that the applicant, namely, the plaintiff had been declared as absolute owner of the property and the premises in question are not enemy property. So, the Deputy Commissioner was requested to look into the matter and make necessary order as per law immediately under intimation to the Secretary of the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Though this letter was issued on 14th November, 1983, it appears that the Deputy Commissioner did not take any step whatsoever for taking further steps in view of the fact that it is not an enemy property which was accepted even by the Chief Martial Law Administrator's office at the relevant time. We may observe that the order from the office of the Chief Martial Law Administrator was binding upon all the authorities subordinate to the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Be that as it may, we express our view that since the highest Court of the country accepted the decree to the effect that the suit property is not an enemy/vested property, the authorities concerned must release the same in favour of the plaintiff who has been declared as legal owner by the court. Considering the above facts and circumstances and the material evidence on record, we are of the view that the plaintiff in this suit is entitled to a part decree only. 

 14. In the result, this appeal is allowed in part and the suit is decreed in part for an amount of Tk. 2,34,000.00 (two lakh thirty four thousand) in pursuance of our findings above with regard to the rent of the premises in question and in the similar way thereafter at the rate of Tk. 6500.00 per month upto the delivery of the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we pass no order as to costs.
